_comment: Deep Time's climate mapping reference (plan §7.2, P1-09). One file, two readers. The core (crates/deeptime-core/src/bake/biomes.rs, include_str!) bakes the five biome inputs against it: 'bands' are OverworldBiomeBuilder's band edges (1.21.1; the JUnit OverworldBandsTest checks them against the class; 'weirdness' holds the slice edges of |weirdness| on the rising branch: valley, low, mid, high, peak), 'reference' is the land distribution of vanilla's own erosion and peaks-and-valleys (the router of minecraft:overworld at seed 0, points on a jittered grid, kept where continents >= land_min_continents; ClimateMappingBuilder measures and logs it). The game ships this file as data/deeptime/deeptime/climate_mapping/default.json: at a Deep Time world's first start ClimateMappingBuilder maps the baked values from the bands and reference the bake recorded (notes.bake.climate.reference) onto the pack's bands (this resource, which a datapack may override) and the pack's own router distribution, and stores the tables in the world data folder as climate_mapping.json.

reference.source: vanilla 1.21.1 minecraft:overworld router (NeoForge 21.1.249 GameTest server, no worldgen mods), seed 0, a 640 x 640 jittered grid over +-60,000 blocks, the first 65,536 points with continents >= -0.19 (of 91,405 tried); measured by ClimateMappingBuilder 2026-09-29
